answer: Each identity must present a sequential state proof whose memory-hardness resists parallel evaluation and whose tenure is soulbound, so a farm cannot split one proof across a thousand machines and cannot hand the result to a fresh account. Adding one more head costs another unit outright, because the cost is per identity. The tide is the sequential proof, the vault the tenure it is bound to, and the cipher the memory-hardness that resists parallel evaluation; the tide and the vault are per identity, and it is the cipher that stops one proof serving a hundred clones.
